name: William H. Francis
role: Associate justice of Dakota Territory, at Bismarck
bio: William H. Francis of Bismarck was nominated associate justice of Dakota Territory in July 1884 after Frank Sperry declined, and that August he gave the address welcoming Governor Pierce to the capital. In September 1885 he presided at the Bismarck trial of the Marquis de Mores, where the paper reported open hostility between him and Prosecuting Attorney T. K. Long, who attacked him in print; the paper itself called on the judge to answer the charges or resign. He held court at Deadwood that fall, staying with the Marquis on the way. In 1886 he issued the Billings County taxpayers' injunction against Stark County tax collection and heard the Refrigerator Car Co.'s tax suits, and that December he dissolved the injunction pro forma so the case could go to the supreme court.
